raw_content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "differentiate_solid_mass_from_vascular_anomaly", "description": "When interpreting a rounded hyperdense lesion in the chest, distinguish between solid masses and vascular anomalies by verifying vascular continuity and enhancement patterns.", "applicable_conditions": "Applies to any medical imaging interpretation task involving rounded or hyperdense pulmonary/mediastinal lesions where differential diagnosis includes both solid tissue (e.g., tumor, granuloma) and vascular structures (e.g., aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm).", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": [], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If a rounded hyperdense lesion is identified: (1) Do NOT diagnose as a vascular anomaly (e.g., pseudoaneurysm) based solely on location and density; (2) Explicitly check for vascular continuity with adjacent vessels on multi-planar reconstructions; (3) Verify presence of contrast enhancement patterns typical of blood flow if contrast was used; (4) If vascular continuity is absent or enhancement is heterogeneous/solid, prioritize solid mass diagnoses (e.g., malignancy, granuloma) over vascular etiologies."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
